source_user: Advanced cluster case cluster scheduling and recovery-69: Design a resilient cluster scheduler for distributed LLM training and inference. Variant 69 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: cover gang scheduling, GPU/NIC/topology-aware placement, fragmentation, preemption, checkpoint cadence, node drain, elastic restart, replica routing, SLOs, and resource accounting. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: each training job declares GPU type/count, DP/TP shape, CPU, memory, storage, NIC/RDMA and NUMA/topology constraints, priority, checkpoint format and cadence; inventory, scheduler events, node health, fencing, restart, inference readiness, routing, and SLO events are observable with synchronized timestamps. Verify these platform-dependent contracts before relying on them.

Hypothesis: atomic topology-aware gang admission with fragmentation accounting, checkpoint-safe preemption, fenced node drain, bounded elastic restart, and readiness-gated replica routing reduces failed starts, lost work, and recovery time without breaching training throughput or inference availability/latency SLOs. Compare current and canary policies at matched scale, workload, inventory, model, traffic, and checkpoint cadence; predefine effect size and rollback thresholds.

Measure gang queue/start latency, requested versus allocated versus used GPU-hours, GPU/NIC/NUMA placement and utilization, fragmentation, preemption and checkpoint age, checkpoint write/restore validation, failure detection-to-fence/drain/restart, replayed samples or tokens, replica readiness, error rate, throughput, and p50/p95/p99 latency. Record units, denominators, topology, sample counts, confidence intervals, and confounders such as workload mix, thermal throttling, network congestion, and inventory changes. Admission must be all-or-nothing; never route to an unready replica or reuse an unfenced node. Roll back the canary on corrupted checkpoints, unsafe fencing, SLO breach, increased lost work, or no improvement after the planned sample size. Use least-privilege diagnostics and redact identifiers; evidence from synthetic failure injection and matched repeated trials is required before claiming resilience.
risks: platform-specific scheduler, fencing, checkpoint, topology, and routing semantics may differ
single-run or unsynchronized measurements could confound causal claims
unsafe node reuse or unready routing could cause data loss or SLO breach
evidence_required: matched baseline and canary traces
repeated controlled node-failure injections
validated checkpoint and synchronized event logs
resource, topology, SLO, and uncertainty reports

Required evidence is synchronized raw events, repeated failure injection, matched baseline, and least-privilege redacted diagnostics.
